title: $500,000 today or $1,000 a month for life?

scenes.text: $500,000 today, or $1,000 a month for the rest of your life. Which one are you taking?
Jake grabs the half million. Mike takes $1,000 a month. Safe. Forever.
Jake invests it, and only takes out 4% a year. That's $20,000 a year, or $1,667 a month.
So Jake gets $1,667 a month. Mike gets $1,000.
And here's the trap. Mike's $1,000 never grows. With 3% inflation, in 25 years, it only buys what $478 buys today.
Want your own number? Take your monthly spending, times 300. Spend $4,000 a month? You need $1.2 million.
So which did you pick? Lump sum, or monthly? Tell me below.

props.disclaimer: The 4% rule is a historical rule of thumb, not a guarantee. Example ignores taxes. Not financial advice.
